Apothecary
uh-POTH-uh-kair-ee
noun
From Greek through Latin and French for storekeeper of spices; in Exodus, the skilled compounder of holy oil and incense.

📖 Biblical Definition

The apothecary in Scripture is the skilled compounder of sacred ointments and perfumes. Moses is commanded to make an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary, and likewise a perfume, a confection after the art of the apothecary, pure and holy. Ecclesiastes later warns that dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour, so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour. The word therefore joins craft, holiness, and moral parable. Holy things required art, measure, and purity; they were not casual mixtures. Reputation likewise is a compounded ointment easily spoiled by small folly. The church should honor skilled work offered to God and fear the fly in the jar. Modern life has pharmacies without holiness and brands without character. Exodus still calls for consecrated skill, and Ecclesiastes still calls for vigilance over a good name. Christ, the Anointed, fulfills what the holy oil signified; His people must not perfume the flesh and call it worship, nor treat a little tolerated folly as a small thing in a man of reputation.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A compounder of ointments; in Torah, the artisan of holy anointing oil and incense; in Ecclesiastes, a parable of spoiled reputation.

expand to see more

APOTHECARY, a maker and keeper of compounds and spices.

Holy anointing oil was made after the art of the apothecary.

Sacred perfume likewise required that art, pure and holy.

Dead flies spoil the apothecary’s ointment.

A little folly spoils a reputation for wisdom.

📖 Key Scripture

Exo 30:25 — "And thou shalt make it an oil of holy ointment, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary: it shall be an holy anointing oil."

Exo 30:35 — "And thou shalt make it a perfume, a confection after the art of the apothecary, tempered together, pure and holy:"

Ecc 10:1 — "Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour."

Exo 37:29 — "And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The apothecary is reduced to a costume word or a shop; Scripture makes him a figure of consecrated skill and of fragile honor.

expand to see more

The corruption is secularizing sacred craft into mere aesthetics, or moralizing Ecclesiastes into brand management without the fear of God. Holy oil was not spa product. Reputation is not influencer capital. Another corruption is careless worship that scorns skill as unspiritual. Exodus required art. The LORD who prescribed the compound still deserves ordered excellence, and the fool who drops flies into the jar still stinks in the gates.

A soft modern form is therapeutic self-care language that treats anointing as wellness. Biblical anointing marks persons and things for God. Keep the apothecary in the sanctuary sense, and the parable will keep its sting.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Apothecary names the skilled compounder of holy oil and incense, and by proverb the keeper of an easily spoiled ointment of honor.

expand to see more

Craft — art of the apothecary in Exodus 30.

Oil — holy anointing oil, compound and sacred.

Incense — perfume tempered pure and holy.

Proverb — dead flies in the ointment.

Christ — the true Anointed fulfilling the sign.

Usage

"Holy ointment was compounded after the art of the apothecary."

"Dead flies cause the apothecary’s ointment to stink."

"A little folly spoils the reputation that wisdom built."
